catalog.title: Ginger chicken and cabbage with rice
catalog.description: Golden chicken, sweet cabbage, and crisp carrots in a light ginger-soy glaze, served beside fluffy rice for a gentle, savory weeknight dinner.
ingredients: 1 pound boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into thin strips
14 ounces bagged shredded green cabbage and carrots, without dressing
instructions: Combine the rice with the measured rice water in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil, cover, and reduce to low. Cook for 18 minutes, then remove from the heat and leave covered for 5 minutes. If your rice package specifies a different water ratio or cook time, follow it and allow that extra time.

While the rice cooks, pat the chicken strips dry. Whisk the measured sauce water with the soy sauce, vinegar, honey, cornstarch, ginger, and garlic until smooth. Keep the cabbage mixture and scallions ready beside the stove.

Heat half the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Spread the chicken in one layer and cook for 6–8 minutes, turning occasionally, until browned and the thickest pieces reach 165°F. Transfer to a clean plate. If the chicken overlaps, cook in two batches and allow extra time.

Add the remaining oil and the cabbage mixture to the skillet. Cook for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until the cabbage softens but the carrots retain a little bite. Stir the sauce again to lift any settled cornstarch, then pour it into the pan.

Return the chicken and any collected juices. Toss over medium heat for 1–2 minutes until the sauce bubbles and lightly coats everything. Fold in the scallions. Fluff the rice and divide it among serving plates with the chicken and vegetables. When scaling up, use another skillet or cook in batches; do not multiply the cooking time or crowd the pan.
catalog.notes: This original Kwilt dinner borrows the quick, staged cooking of Chinese home stir-fries without claiming to be a traditional named dish. Bagged cabbage and carrots keep preparation manageable; a small amount of ginger-soy sauce coats rather than floods the vegetables. Rice cooks alongside the skillet, so the meal does not depend on leftovers or an uncounted side. Allow about 20 minutes of hands-on work within the 35-minute total.

catalog.title: Chicken Parmesan cutlets with green beans and couscous
catalog.description: Oven-crisp chicken cutlets with tomato sauce and melted mozzarella, roasted green beans, and fluffy couscous to catch the juices.
ingredients: 4 thin chicken breast cutlets, 5 ounces each and 1/2 inch thick
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the upper middle. Lightly oil a large rimmed sheet pan with one ninth of the measured oil. Mix the panko, Parmesan, Italian seasoning, and pepper on a plate. Brush the cutlets with one third of the measured oil and sprinkle with half the salt, then press into the crumbs on both sides.

Arrange the cutlets with space between them on one side of the sheet pan. Toss the green beans with the remaining oil and spread beside the chicken. Roast for 15 minutes; turn the beans and check the chicken. The crumbs should be golden and the chicken almost cooked through.

Spoon the marinara over the centers of the cutlets, leaving crumbed edges exposed, and scatter the mozzarella over the sauce. Return to the oven for 5–8 minutes, until the cheese melts and the thickest part of each cutlet reaches 165°F. Remove individual cutlets sooner if needed; leave firm beans in the oven until tender.

Meanwhile, bring the water and remaining salt to a boil in a small saucepan. Stir in the couscous, cover, and remove from the heat. Let stand for 5 minutes, then fluff. Use the package water ratio if it differs; choose plain quick-cooking couscous, not pearl couscous.

Divide the couscous and green beans among serving plates and add one cutlet to each. When increasing servings, use an additional sheet pan so the chicken and beans remain in a single layer; rotate pans if they occupy different oven racks.
catalog.notes: A weeknight interpretation of Italian-American chicken Parmesan, built as a complete meal. Oven cooking and purchased marinara limit hands-on work to about 20 minutes, with vegetables roasting alongside. Thin, evenly sized cutlets and a thermometer matter more than the clock; this version does not promise the same crust as shallow-fried restaurant chicken.

catalog.title: Orange chicken with snap peas and rice
catalog.description: Tender chicken and crisp snap peas in a bright orange glaze, with steamed rice to make a complete, mild family supper.
ingredients: 1 1/4 pounds boneless skinless chicken breast, cut into 3/4-inch pieces
instructions: Start the rice in a covered saucepan with the measured water. Bring to a boil, reduce the heat to low, and cook for 18 minutes. Remove from the heat and rest, still covered, for 5 minutes. Follow the package ratio if it differs, allowing extra time for a longer-cooking rice.

While the rice cooks, whisk the orange juice, zest, soy sauce, vinegar, honey, cornstarch, and ginger in a bowl. Pat the chicken pieces dry. Keep the sauce and snap peas next to the stove before cooking.

Heat the oil in a wide 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Arrange the chicken in one layer. Cook for 7–9 minutes, turning occasionally, until the pieces are lightly golden and reach 165°F. Transfer to a clean plate; cook in batches and allow extra time if the pan is crowded.

Add the snap peas to the skillet and cook for 2–3 minutes, stirring, until bright green with a slight bite. Rewhisk the orange sauce, pour it into the pan, and lower the heat to medium. Simmer for 2 minutes until the sauce turns glossy and coats a spoon.

Return the chicken and its juices and toss for 1 minute to coat and heat through. Fluff the rice and serve with the chicken and snap peas. The glaze should cling lightly rather than set like jelly. For larger yields, use another skillet or work in batches rather than piling everything into one pan.
catalog.notes: An original weeknight take on Chinese-American orange chicken. It uses orange zest as well as juice for fragrance and skips batter to keep the method and cleanup simple. Snap peas supply crunch, and rice is included in the schedule rather than assumed to be ready. The result is glazed chicken, not a crispy fried takeout replica; allow about 20 minutes of hands-on work.

research.adaptationDecision: Original mild, unbreaded skillet dinner with a defined rice schedule, snap peas, and a restrained honey-orange glaze. No copied source method, invented reviewer consensus, or kitchen-test claim.

catalog.title: Chicken Marsala with peas and egg noodles
catalog.description: Golden chicken cutlets in a savory mushroom-Marsala sauce, spooned over tender egg noodles and sweet peas.
ingredients: 4 chicken breast cutlets, 5 ounces each and 1/4 inch thick
instructions: Set a large saucepan of the measured water over high heat. Pat the cutlets dry and season with half the salt and the pepper. Dust with flour, shaking excess back onto the plate; discard the leftover flour after it has touched raw chicken.

Heat the oil and half the butter in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the thin cutlets for 3–4 minutes per side, until golden and 165°F in the thickest part. Transfer to a clean plate. If they do not fit in one layer, use two batches and allow extra time.

Add the remaining butter and the mushrooms to the skillet. Cook for 5–6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the mushrooms have released their liquid and begun to brown. Move the pan off the burner, pour in the Marsala, then return to medium heat. Simmer for 3–4 minutes to reduce by about half, scraping up browned bits.

Add the broth, cream, and remaining salt. Simmer gently, uncovered, for 6–8 minutes until the sauce lightly coats a spoon. Meanwhile, boil the noodles according to their package, adding the frozen peas during the final 3 minutes. Drain the noodles and peas together.

Return the chicken and collected juices to the mushroom sauce and warm gently for 1–2 minutes. Divide the noodles and peas among serving plates, add the cutlets, and spoon over the sauce. When scaling, preserve the pan space and reduce the sauce by its appearance rather than multiplying the cooking time.
catalog.notes: Chicken Marsala belongs to Italian-American home and restaurant cooking. This complete supper keeps the defining fortified-wine and mushroom sauce while adding peas and egg noodles within the stated time. Pre-sliced mushrooms and purchased thin cutlets keep hands-on work around 20 minutes. Marsala is an alcoholic ingredient; a short reduction does not make the dish alcohol-free.

catalog.title: Chicken florentine with lemon orzo
catalog.description: Tender chicken cutlets nestled in creamy lemon orzo with plenty of spinach and a savory Parmesan finish.
ingredients: 4 chicken breast cutlets, 5 ounces each and 1/2 inch thick
instructions: Pat the chicken dry and season with half the salt and the pepper. Heat the oil in a wide, deep lidded skillet over medium-high heat. Brown the cutlets for 3 minutes per side, then transfer to a plate; they will finish cooking with the orzo.

Lower the heat to medium. Add the garlic and stir for 20 seconds, then add the orzo and stir for 1 minute. Pour in the broth and scrape the bottom of the pan. Bring to a simmer, stir in the cream and remaining salt, and return the chicken and any juices.

Cover and simmer gently for 10–12 minutes. Stir under the chicken every few minutes so the orzo does not stick. Check that the pasta is tender and the chicken reaches 165°F. Remove a finished cutlet if the pasta needs longer, or simmer a little longer if either is not ready. If the pan dries before the pasta softens, add a small splash of water.

Transfer the cooked chicken to a clean plate. Add the spinach to the orzo in two handfuls, stirring for 2–3 minutes until wilted. Remove from the heat and stir in the Parmesan, lemon juice, and zest. The orzo should be creamy and spoonable; loosen with a little water if needed.

Return the chicken to the pan and serve one cutlet with a proportional serving of the spinach-orzo mixture. For larger yields, use two pans rather than stacking the chicken; check pasta absorption and chicken temperature independently.
catalog.notes: Florentine-style dishes commonly pair a main ingredient with spinach. This original Kwilt version folds the spinach into lemony orzo, making the starch and vegetable part of the same pan. It uses broth and lemon instead of wine and is not presented as a traditional recipe from Florence. Hands-on work is estimated at 18–20 minutes; keep an eye on the orzo because pan width affects evaporation.

catalog.title: Chicken enchilada skillet with black beans
catalog.description: A bubbling skillet of chicken, black beans, peppers, and tender corn-tortilla pieces in mild red sauce, finished with melted cheese.
ingredients: 2 cups shredded cooked rotisserie chicken, skin and bones removed
1 can (15 ounces) black beans, rinsed and drained
6 small corn tortillas, cut into wide strips
instructions: Heat the oil in a deep 12-inch lidded skillet over medium heat. Add the bell pepper and cook for 5 minutes until softened. Stir in the cumin for 20 seconds.

Add the cooked chicken, drained beans, frozen corn, enchilada sauce, and water. Stir and bring to a steady simmer. Cook for 5–6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chicken and sauce are steaming hot and the chicken reaches 165°F.

Fold in the tortilla strips until coated, then simmer gently for 3–4 minutes. Turn them carefully once so they soften without breaking down into paste. The skillet should be thick and spoonable rather than dry.
Scatter the Monterey Jack over the top, cover, and reduce the heat to low. Cook for 2–3 minutes until the cheese melts. Meanwhile, stir the yogurt and lime juice together in a small bowl.

Divide the skillet among shallow serving bowls and add the lime yogurt. This timing assumes purchased cooked chicken; cooking raw chicken first adds time. For larger batches, use a wider pan or two skillets and confirm the filling heats through before adding tortillas.
catalog.notes: This is an original Tex-Mex-inspired tortilla skillet rather than rolled traditional enchiladas. Purchased cooked chicken, canned beans, and mild prepared sauce keep the whole meal within about 30 minutes. The pepper and corn provide vegetables without a separate side, and the stovetop cheese finish avoids an oven transfer. The tortillas soften into the sauce; they are not intended to stay crisp.

catalog.title: Chicken tortilla soup with avocado
catalog.description: Tomato broth, tender chicken, black beans and corn under a crunchy tortilla topping.
ingredients: 1 can (15 ounces) black beans, rinsed and drained
instructions: Heat the oil in a large soup pot over medium heat. Soften the onion for 5 minutes, then stir in the cumin for 30 seconds.
Add tomatoes with their juices, broth and beans. Bring to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes, stirring once or twice.
Add corn and chicken. Return to a simmer for 5–7 minutes until the corn is tender and the chicken reaches 165°F. Add a splash of water if the broth has reduced too far.
Remove from heat and add lime juice. Divide among serving bowls and finish with avocado and crushed tortilla chips just before eating.
catalog.notes: A broth-based Tex-Mex-inspired supper distinct from the tortilla skillet: crunchy chips and cool avocado remain separate until serving. Estimated hands-on work: 15 minutes. catalog.title: Chicken pesto flatbreads with tomato salad
catalog.description: Crisp flatbreads topped with chicken, basil pesto and melted mozzarella, with juicy tomato salad.
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F. Arrange naan on two baking sheets. Divide the pesto evenly over them, leaving the rim clear.
Divide chicken, half the spinach and mozzarella over the breads. Keep toppings in an even thin layer so the center heats through.
Bake for 10–14 minutes, switching sheet positions halfway, until cheese bubbles, edges are crisp and chicken reaches 165°F.
Toss tomatoes and remaining spinach with vinegar, oil and salt. Cut the hot flatbreads into wedges and serve immediately alongside the salad.
catalog.notes: Purchased naan supplies a crisp dinner base without dough preparation; spinach is divided between the hot topping and fresh side. Estimated hands-on work: 15 minutes. catalog.title: Chicken and sweetcorn chowder
catalog.description: A creamy potato-and-corn supper with tender chicken and a gentle thyme aroma.
ingredients: 1 pound Yukon Gold potatoes, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
instructions: Melt butter in a large pot over medium heat. Cook onion and celery for 5 minutes, stirring until softened.
Add potatoes, broth and thyme. Bring to a simmer, cover loosely and cook 12–15 minutes until a knife easily enters the potatoes.
Whisk the flour into cold milk until smooth. Stir into the soup with corn and chicken; simmer gently for 5–7 minutes, stirring, until thickened and chicken reaches 165°F.
Mash a few potatoes against the pot to thicken further if desired. Divide into serving bowls and serve with the rolls; do not boil hard after adding milk.
catalog.notes: Potato and flour supply body without canned soup; cooked chicken shortens the schedule while rolls make the portions dinner-sized. Estimated hands-on work: 18 minutes. catalog.title: Turkey cheeseburger skillet pasta
catalog.description: Tender pasta shells, savory turkey and sweet peas in a creamy tomato-cheddar sauce.
instructions: Heat oil in a deep lidded skillet. Cook turkey and onion over medium-high heat for 7–8 minutes, breaking up the meat until it reaches 165°F.

Add peas for the final 3 minutes. Check that the pasta is tender; add water a splash at a time if it dries before cooking through.
Take off the heat. Stir in cheddar, mustard, pickles and pepper until creamy. Let stand 2 minutes and spoon into serving bowls.

catalog.title: Turkey zucchini taco boats
catalog.description: Tender zucchini boats filled with mildly seasoned turkey, beans and melted cheese.
ingredients: 1 can (15 ounces) black beans, rinsed and drained
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F. Halve zucchini lengthwise and scoop out centers, leaving 1/4-inch walls. Chop the removed flesh. Place boats in a large baking dish with water, cover with foil and bake 12 minutes while preparing the filling.

Heat oil in a skillet. Cook turkey for 7–8 minutes, breaking it apart, until 165°F. Add chopped zucchini, cumin and paprika; cook 3 minutes. Stir in beans and salsa and simmer 3 minutes until not watery.
Carefully uncover the boats, drain excess water and fill with the turkey mixture, mounding it evenly. Scatter cheese over top and bake uncovered for 10–12 minutes until zucchini is easily pierced.
Wrap tortillas in a damp paper towel and microwave 30–60 seconds. Serve two boats per person with two tortillas and any filling that did not fit alongside.
catalog.notes: Prebaking zucchini while cooking turkey avoids long assembly time; beans and tortillas make this a full dinner rather than a low-starch side. Estimated hands-on work: 20 minutes. ingredients: 1 pound chicken breast cutlets, 1/2 inch thick

Lower heat and stir in cream and Parmesan. Warm gently for 1 minute; if too thick, stir in a splash of water before serving.
catalog.notes: Hands-on estimate: 20 minutes or less. One deep skillet. Contains wheat and milk; check gnocchi for egg. Scale ingredients proportionally; for more than four servings use a second pan or cook in batches, allowing extra time. Keep food in a shallow layer for browning; do not double simmering time. Check tenderness and temperature, not the clock.
kitchenTestNotes: Original formulation reviewed on paper; not kitchen-tested. Use shelf-stable potato gnocchi with a short package cooking time.

catalog.title: Mushroom cheese omelets with bean salad

instructions: Toss beans, tomatoes, scallions and parsley with half the oil, half the lemon juice and half the salt. Set aside.

Lower heat to medium-low and add a little of the remaining oil. Pour in half the eggs, tilt to coat and gently lift edges for liquid egg to flow beneath. Cook 3 to 4 minutes until just set, then add half the mushrooms and cheddar to one half.

Fold and cook 1 minute until eggs are fully set and cheese melts. Slide onto a plate and cut in half. recipes.title: Ginger chicken and cabbage with rice

researchTask.description: Golden chicken, sweet cabbage, and crisp carrots in a light ginger-soy glaze, served beside fluffy rice for a gentle, savory weeknight dinner.
ingredients: 1 pound boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into thin strips
14 ounces bagged shredded green cabbage and carrots, without dressing
instructions: Combine the rice with the measured rice water in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil, cover, and reduce to low. Cook for 18 minutes, then remove from the heat and leave covered for 5 minutes. If your rice package specifies a different water ratio or cook time, follow it and allow that extra time.

While the rice cooks, pat the chicken strips dry. Whisk the measured sauce water with the soy sauce, vinegar, honey, cornstarch, ginger, and garlic until smooth. Keep the cabbage mixture and scallions ready beside the stove.

Heat half the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Spread the chicken in one layer and cook for 6–8 minutes, turning occasionally, until browned and the thickest pieces reach 165°F. Transfer to a clean plate. If the chicken overlaps, cook in two batches and allow extra time.

Add the remaining oil and the cabbage mixture to the skillet. Cook for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until the cabbage softens but the carrots retain a little bite. Stir the sauce again to lift any settled cornstarch, then pour it into the pan.

Return the chicken and any collected juices. Toss over medium heat for 1–2 minutes until the sauce bubbles and lightly coats everything. Fold in the scallions. Fluff the rice and divide it among serving plates with the chicken and vegetables. When scaling up, use another skillet or cook in batches; do not multiply the cooking time or crowd the pan.
researchTask.notes: This original Kwilt dinner borrows the quick, staged cooking of Chinese home stir-fries without claiming to be a traditional named dish. Bagged cabbage and carrots keep preparation manageable; a small amount of ginger-soy sauce coats rather than floods the vegetables. Rice cooks alongside the skillet, so the meal does not depend on leftovers or an uncounted side. Allow about 20 minutes of hands-on work within the 35-minute total.

recipes.title: Chicken Parmesan cutlets with green beans and couscous

researchTask.description: Oven-crisp chicken cutlets with tomato sauce and melted mozzarella, roasted green beans, and fluffy couscous to catch the juices.
ingredients: 4 thin chicken breast cutlets, 5 ounces each and 1/2 inch thick
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the upper middle. Lightly oil a large rimmed sheet pan with one ninth of the measured oil. Mix the panko, Parmesan, Italian seasoning, and pepper on a plate. Brush the cutlets with one third of the measured oil and sprinkle with half the salt, then press into the crumbs on both sides.

Arrange the cutlets with space between them on one side of the sheet pan. Toss the green beans with the remaining oil and spread beside the chicken. Roast for 15 minutes; turn the beans and check the chicken. The crumbs should be golden and the chicken almost cooked through.

Spoon the marinara over the centers of the cutlets, leaving crumbed edges exposed, and scatter the mozzarella over the sauce. Return to the oven for 5–8 minutes, until the cheese melts and the thickest part of each cutlet reaches 165°F. Remove individual cutlets sooner if needed; leave firm beans in the oven until tender.

Meanwhile, bring the water and remaining salt to a boil in a small saucepan. Stir in the couscous, cover, and remove from the heat. Let stand for 5 minutes, then fluff. Use the package water ratio if it differs; choose plain quick-cooking couscous, not pearl couscous.

Divide the couscous and green beans among serving plates and add one cutlet to each. When increasing servings, use an additional sheet pan so the chicken and beans remain in a single layer; rotate pans if they occupy different oven racks.
researchTask.notes: A weeknight interpretation of Italian-American chicken Parmesan, built as a complete meal. Oven cooking and purchased marinara limit hands-on work to about 20 minutes, with vegetables roasting alongside. Thin, evenly sized cutlets and a thermometer matter more than the clock; this version does not promise the same crust as shallow-fried restaurant chicken.

recipes.title: Orange chicken with snap peas and rice

researchTask.description: Tender chicken and crisp snap peas in a bright orange glaze, with steamed rice to make a complete, mild family supper.
ingredients: 1 1/4 pounds boneless skinless chicken breast, cut into 3/4-inch pieces
instructions: Start the rice in a covered saucepan with the measured water. Bring to a boil, reduce the heat to low, and cook for 18 minutes. Remove from the heat and rest, still covered, for 5 minutes. Follow the package ratio if it differs, allowing extra time for a longer-cooking rice.

While the rice cooks, whisk the orange juice, zest, soy sauce, vinegar, honey, cornstarch, and ginger in a bowl. Pat the chicken pieces dry. Keep the sauce and snap peas next to the stove before cooking.

Heat the oil in a wide 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Arrange the chicken in one layer. Cook for 7–9 minutes, turning occasionally, until the pieces are lightly golden and reach 165°F. Transfer to a clean plate; cook in batches and allow extra time if the pan is crowded.

Add the snap peas to the skillet and cook for 2–3 minutes, stirring, until bright green with a slight bite. Rewhisk the orange sauce, pour it into the pan, and lower the heat to medium. Simmer for 2 minutes until the sauce turns glossy and coats a spoon.

Return the chicken and its juices and toss for 1 minute to coat and heat through. Fluff the rice and serve with the chicken and snap peas. The glaze should cling lightly rather than set like jelly. For larger yields, use another skillet or work in batches rather than piling everything into one pan.
researchTask.notes: An original weeknight take on Chinese-American orange chicken. It uses orange zest as well as juice for fragrance and skips batter to keep the method and cleanup simple. recipes.title: Chicken Marsala with peas and egg noodles

researchTask.description: Golden chicken cutlets in a savory mushroom-Marsala sauce, spooned over tender egg noodles and sweet peas.
ingredients: 4 chicken breast cutlets, 5 ounces each and 1/4 inch thick
instructions: Set a large saucepan of the measured water over high heat. Pat the cutlets dry and season with half the salt and the pepper. Dust with flour, shaking excess back onto the plate; discard the leftover flour after it has touched raw chicken.

Heat the oil and half the butter in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the thin cutlets for 3–4 minutes per side, until golden and 165°F in the thickest part. Transfer to a clean plate. If they do not fit in one layer, use two batches and allow extra time.

Add the remaining butter and the mushrooms to the skillet. Cook for 5–6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the mushrooms have released their liquid and begun to brown. Move the pan off the burner, pour in the Marsala, then return to medium heat. Simmer for 3–4 minutes to reduce by about half, scraping up browned bits.

Add the broth, cream, and remaining salt. Simmer gently, uncovered, for 6–8 minutes until the sauce lightly coats a spoon. Meanwhile, boil the noodles according to their package, adding the frozen peas during the final 3 minutes. Drain the noodles and peas together.

Return the chicken and collected juices to the mushroom sauce and warm gently for 1–2 minutes. Divide the noodles and peas among serving plates, add the cutlets, and spoon over the sauce. When scaling, preserve the pan space and reduce the sauce by its appearance rather than multiplying the cooking time.
researchTask.notes: Chicken Marsala belongs to Italian-American home and restaurant cooking. This complete supper keeps the defining fortified-wine and mushroom sauce while adding peas and egg noodles within the stated time. instructions: Heat the oil in a deep 12-inch lidded skillet over medium heat. Add the bell pepper and cook for 5 minutes until softened. Stir in the cumin for 20 seconds.

Scatter the Monterey Jack over the top, cover, and reduce the heat to low. Cook for 2–3 minutes until the cheese melts. Meanwhile, stir the yogurt and lime juice together in a small bowl.

Divide the skillet among shallow serving bowls and add the lime yogurt. This timing assumes purchased cooked chicken; cooking raw chicken first adds time. For larger batches, use a wider pan or two skillets and confirm the filling heats through before adding tortillas.
researchTask.notes: This is an original Tex-Mex-inspired tortilla skillet rather than rolled traditional enchiladas.
